To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the exon-3 domain of IL-1SRalpha is important for the stabilization of high-affinity IL15.IL-1SRalpha complex and (2) a soluble IL-15 receptor sushi domain containing a peptide corresponding to the exon-3 of IL-15 Ralpha is a dual IL-15 receptor antagonist and agonist.

the exon-2-encoded IL-15R alpha sushi domain is required for IL-15 binding to IL-15R beta/gamma, whereas the exon-3 encoded IL-15R alpaha N-terminal peptide is required for IL15 binding to IL15R alpha/beta/gamma.

the 13- to 15-aa peptide encoded by exon 3 of the IL-15Ra gene contributes to high-affinity binding of IL-15 to IL-15Rα and that this peptide is crucial for the antagonistic effect displayed by the natural soluble form of IL-15Ra.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new concept in cytokine biology, that is, the existence of a cytokine receptor antagonist that can act as a full agonist of the receptor for another cytokine of the same family.
the molecular determinants of the antagonistic effect exerted by soluble IL-15 Ralpha on the IL-15.
the elucidation of the molecular basis of the agonistic and antagonistic properties of the soluble IL15Ralpha sushi domains.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the exon-2-encoded domain of IL15Ralpha is crucial for the antagonistic effect, whereas the exon-3 encoded domain is crucial for the high-affinity binding.

the exon-2- and exon-3-encoded domains of the IL-15 receptor alpha chain contribute to the high-affinity binding of IL-15, but the exon-3 domain also contributes to the antagonistic effect exerted on IL-15 action by sIL-15 Ralpha through the IL-15 Ralpha/beta/gammac complex.

the exon-2-encoded domain of IL15Ralpha (the sushi domain) is crucial for IL-15 high affinity binding and for the agonistic effect of the sushi domain, whereas the exon-3 encoded domain is crucial for the antagonistic effect.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the exon-1-encoded sushi domain and the exon-3 encoded 13-aa N-terminal peptide of IL-15Ralpaha are the key domains that are required for the stabilization of IL-15 high affinity binding and for the antagonistic effect, respectively.
the 13- aa exon-3-encoded peptide of the soluble IL15Ralpha ectodomain is crucial for the antagonistic effect on IL-15 action, whereas the exon-2-encoded domain is crucial for agonistic effect.

the exon-2-encoded domain and the N-terminal 13-aa sequence of the exon-3 domain are both important for the stabilization of IL-15 high affinity binding to IL-15R, and for the IL-2-like agonistic activity of IL-15 in IL-15R beta/gamma.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IL-15Ralphas with a sushi domain are agonists, whereas IL-15Ralfa species with the exon-3 domain are antagonists, and this is due to their respective affinites to IL-15.

the exon-2-encoded domain and the exon-3 encoded domain of IL- 15Ralpha are both important for the IL- 15 high- affinity binding and for the antagonistic effect, and that they act through distinct mechanisms.
the exon-2-encoded domain and, to a much lesser extent, the exon-3 domain contribute to the high-affinity interaction of IL-15 with IL-15Ralphabeta/gamma.
